title: Avionics Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
15.     MOS 6391, Avionics Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. Avionics Chiefs, as staff noncommissioned officers in
charge of the avionics department supervise the maintenance and repair of
aircraft avionics systems, equipment and components at the IMA/OMA levels.
At the intermediate maintenance activity (MALS), the Avionics Chief (MGySgt)
serves as the OccFld sponsor for all 63/6400 MOS within the MAG. At the
organizational maintenance activity, the Avionics Chief holds the




                                           3-412                        Enclosure (1)
 3141                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



responsibility of managing the tier III EKMS account/assets as well as
manages avionics manpower within the unit.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must have normal color perception.

            (3) Must possess an EL score of 105 or higher.

            (4) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Must satisfy the requirements for one of the PMOSs within the
6300 or 6400 OccFlds.

        (2) Upon promotion to the rank of master sergeant, should attend and
successfully complete the Avionics Officer/Avionics Chief Foundation Course
(N2362X2) at NAS Pensacola, FL.

       d.   Duties

            (1) MGySgt and MSgt:

            (a) Provides subject matter expertise to appropriate 63XX and
64XX lower level MOSs and input on career progression of all Marines in their
charge.

            (b) Demonstrates a thorough working knowledge of COMNAVAIRFORINST
4790.2 and 3M procedures.

            (c) Ensures facilities are organized to support the maintenance
and repair of avionics systems, equipment, or components at the IMA/OMA
levels.

            (d) Supervise the requisition of spare/replacement parts and
necessary work center supplies and equipment using publications and supply
documents.

            (e) Maintains appropriate records of all maintenance and
inspection actions performed, technical training conducted, and organic
equipment assigned to the avionics department.

            (f) Possesses a thorough understanding and working knowledge of
sound management principles, work center supervision, proper methods of
training personnel, and accepted and approved avionics maintenance
procedures.

            (g) Pursues Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement (DAWIA)
Certification in order to gain qualifications prior to entering senior
billets within the MOS. Marines serving in billets coded with an additional
skill designator (ASD) MOS 8060 as per the table of organization must attain
the appropriate certification level through the Defense Acquisition
University (DAU) within 24 months of billet assignment. The three primary
areas of study typically applicable to AVLOG are:




                                           3-413                        Enclosure (1)
 3141                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



                    1.    Life Cycle Logistics (LCL).

                    2.    Production, Quality, Manufacturing (PQM).

                    3.    Program Management (PM).

            (2) MGySgt:

            (a) Possesses a thorough understanding and working knowledge of
Marine Corps administrative procedures including the format, preparation, and
submission of naval messages.

            (b) Demonstrates a thorough understanding of Marine Corps
aviation staff organization and functioning of the Marine Aviation Logistic
Squadron, Marine Aircraft Wing, and FMF Headquarters levels.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
First-line Supervisors/Managers of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers 49-
1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.




                                         3-414                         Enclosure (1)
 3142                                                                   NAVMC 1200.1L
common_text: The avionics OccFld includes direct and indirect support of all aviation weapon systems. While there is a large similarity in the skills required to provide this support, the systems being supported are diverse. The following examples are provided: direct support repair accomplished at the organizational maintenance activity (OMA) which is normally accomplished on aircraft, e.g., replacement of the radar antenna on the aircraft, indirect support-repair accomplished at the intermediate maintenance activity (IMA) which is normally accomplished off aircraft, e.g., radar system module repair, and repair/calibration of the radar support equipment. Marines entering the OccFld receive MOS 6300, Basic Avionics Marine, and then progress through specific hard skill MOSs and ultimately are assigned MOS 6391, Avionics Chief. Qualifications initially include technical proficiency in the repair of one or more electronic systems after completion of formal training. As the Marine is promoted, repair and administrative requirements for multiple systems take on an equal importance until the Marine is ultimately placed in a supervisory position. Billets for both repair and administration are varied and extend from the squadron level to staff positions at the Wing and force commander, and Headquarters U.S. Marine Corps level.

matches: Maintain and coordinate repair of marine machinery and equipment for installation on vessels.
As the Marine is promoted, repair and administrative requirements for multiple systems take on an equal importance until the Marine is ultimately placed in a supervisory position.
Coordinate work with that of engineers, technicians, and other aircraft maintenance personnel.

Avionics Chiefs, as staff noncommissioned officers in charge of the avionics department supervise the maintenance and repair of aircraft avionics systems, equipment and components at the IMA/OMA levels.

Maintain, repair, and rebuild aircraft structures, functional components, and parts, such as wings and fuselage, rigging, hydraulic units, oxygen systems, fuel systems, electrical systems, gaskets, or seals.
(c) Ensures facilities are organized to support the maintenance and repair of avionics systems, equipment, or components at the IMA/OMA levels.
Requisition and issue equipment and supplies.

Maintain records of equipment maintenance work or repairs.
(e) Maintains appropriate records of all maintenance and inspection actions performed, technical training conducted, and organic equipment assigned to the avionics department.
Analyze training programs and conduct oral and written examinations to ensure the competency of persons operating, installing, and repairing aircraft equipment.

(f) Possesses a thorough understanding and working knowledge of sound management principles, work center supervision, proper methods of training personnel, and accepted and approved avionics maintenance procedures.
Teach company regulations and procedures to other pilots.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
